types.name: __TypeKind
types.description:
GraphQL type kind

The GraphQL specification defines a number of type kinds - the meta type of a type.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description:
## Scalar types

Scalar types appear as the leaf nodes of GraphQL queries. Strings, numbers, and booleans are the built in types, and while it's possible to define your own, it's relatively uncommon.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description:
## Object types

The most common type to be implemented by users. Objects have fields and can implement interfaces.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description:
## Interface types

Interface types are used to represent overlapping fields between multiple types, and can be queried for their concrete type.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description:
## Union types

Unions are similar to interfaces but can not contain any fields on their own.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description:
## Enum types

Like scalars, enum types appear as the leaf nodes of GraphQL queries.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description:
## Input objects

Represents complex values provided in queries _into_ the system.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description:
## List types

Represent lists of other types. This library provides implementations for vectors and slices, but other Rust types can be extended to serve as GraphQL lists.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description:
## Non-null types

In GraphQL, nullable types are the default. By putting a `!` after a type, it becomes non-nullable.

inputFields.name: targetSeries
inputFields.description:
When an event is moved from one series to another,
this field is used to specify the new series.

types.name: UpdatedRealmName
types.description: Exactly one of `plain` or `block` has to be non-null.

types.name: Block
types.description: A `Block`: a UI element that belongs to a realm.

types.name: Node
types.description: A node with a globally unique ID. Mostly useful for relay.

types.name: ByteSpan
types.description: A byte range, encoded as two hex numbers separated by `-`.

types.name: DateTime
types.description:
Combined date and time (with time zone) in [RFC 3339][0] format.

Represents a description of an exact instant on the time-line (such as the
instant that a user account was created).

[`DateTime` scalar][1] compliant.

See also [`chrono::DateTime`][2] for details.

[0]: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339#section-5
[1]: https://graphql-scalars.dev/docs/scalars/date-time
[2]: https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/struct.DateTime.html

types.name: ExtraMetadata
types.description: Arbitrary metadata for events/series. Serialized as JSON object.

types.name: ID
types.description: An opaque, globally-unique identifier

types.name: OpencastId
types.description:
Wrapper around Opencast IDs.
Should prevent using a regular String where an Opencast ID is expected.

types.name: TranslatedString
types.description: A string specified in different languages. Entry 'default' is required.

types.name: AclItem
types.description: A role being granted permission to perform certain actions.

fields.name: role
fields.description: Role. In arrays of AclItems, no two items have the same `role`.

fields.name: actions
fields.description:
List of actions this role can perform (e.g. `read`, `write`,
`annotate`). This is a set, i.e. no duplicate elements.

fields.name: info
fields.description:
Additional info we have about the role. Is `null` if the role is
unknown. For the built-in roles `ROLE_ANONYMOUS`, `ROLE_ADMIN` and
`ROLE_USER`, this might be `null` as well (in which case there is
special handling in the frontend), but might be non-null if custom info
is configured.

fields.name: readRoles
fields.description: This doesn't contain `ROLE_ADMIN` as that is included implicitly.

fields.name: writeRoles
fields.description: This doesn't contain `ROLE_ADMIN` as that is included implicitly.

fields.name: previewRoles
fields.description: This doesn't contain `ROLE_ADMIN` as that is included implicitly.

fields.name: authorizedData
fields.description: Returns the authorized event data if the user has read access or is authenticated for the event.

fields.name: canWrite
fields.description: Whether the current user has write access to this event.

fields.name: workflowStatus
fields.description: Whether the event has active workflows.

fields.name: hostRealms
fields.description: Returns a list of realms where this event is referenced (via some kind of block).

fields.name: hasPassword
fields.description: Whether this event is password protected.

fields.name: isReferencedByRealm
fields.description:
Returns `true` if the realm has a video block with this video
OR if the realm has a series or playlist block including this video.
Otherwise, `false` is returned.

fields.name: jwtForRead
fields.description:
Returns a JWT that grants read access to static files of this event.
Returns `null` if the user does not have access to the event.

fields.name: jwtForDownload
fields.description:
Returns a JWT to create a download link (JWT just grants read access).
Returns `null` if the user does not have access to the event.

types.name: AuthorizedEventData
types.description:
Represents event data that is only accessible for users with read access
and event-specific authenticated users.

types.name: AuthorizedPlaylist
types.description: Represents an Opencast playlist.

fields.name: numEntries
fields.description:
Returns the number of entries in this playlist. Note: this is lazily loaded
and only available in certain contexts (e.g., playlist listings).

fields.name: thumbnailStack
fields.description:
Returns a stack of thumbnails from the events in this playlist.
This is lazily loaded and pre-loaded in certain contexts (like in `load_writable_for_user`).
In other contexts the thumbnails will be fetched from the database on demand.

fields.name: isReferencedByRealm
fields.description:
Returns `true` if the realm has a playlist block with this playlist.
Otherwise, `false` is returned.

fields.name: canWrite
fields.description: Whether the current user has write access to this playlist.

fields.name: dummy
fields.description:
Unused dummy field for this marker type. GraphQL requires all objects to
have at least one field. Always returns `null`.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: How long searching took in ms.

types.name: KnownGroup
types.description:
A group selectable in the ACL UI. Basically a mapping from role to a nice
label and info about the relationship to other roles/groups.

fields.name: dummy
fields.description:
Unused dummy field for this marker type. GraphQL requires all objects to
have at least one field. Always returns `null`.

fields.name: addRealm
fields.description: Adds a new realm.

fields.name: createMyUserRealm
fields.description: Creates the current users realm. Errors if it already exists.

fields.name: createPlaceholderEvent
fields.description:
Creates a placeholder event in the DB when a video is uploaded.
With that, the event can be listed on the "My videos" page before
its processing in Opencast is finished and the event is synced.

fields.name: deleteEvent
fields.description:
Deletes the given event. Meaning: a deletion request is sent to Opencast, the event
is marked as "deletion pending" in Tobira, and fully removed once Opencast
finished deleting the event.

Returns the deletion timestamp in case of success and errors otherwise.
Note that "success" in this case only means the request was successfully sent
and accepted, not that the deletion itself succeeded, which is instead checked
in subsequent harvesting results.

Special case: When a `waiting` event is deleted, this also sends a delete request to OC
but removes the event completely from our DB, regardless of that request's response.

fields.name: updateEventAcl
fields.description:
Updates the acl of a given event by sending the changes to Opencast.
The `acl` parameter can include `read` and `write` roles, as these are the
only roles that can be assigned in frontend for now. `preview` and
`custom_actions` will be added in the future.
If successful, the updated ACL are stored in Tobira without waiting for an upcoming sync - however
this means it might get overwritten again if the update in Opencast failed for some reason.
This solution should be improved in the future.

fields.name: updateEventMetadata
fields.description:
Updates the title and description of an event. A request for this is sent to Opencast,
and the event is optimistically updated in Tobira's DB.

fields.name: deleteSeries
fields.description:
Deletes the given series by sending a delete request to Opencast.
The series is marked as "deletion pending" in Tobira and fully removed once Opencast
finished deleting the series.

Returns the preliminary deletion timestamp.

fields.name: updateSeriesAcl
fields.description:
Updates the acl of a given series by sending the changes to Opencast.
The `acl` parameter can include `read` and `write` roles.
If successful, the updated ACL are stored in Tobira without waiting for an upcoming sync - however
this means it might get overwritten again if the update in Opencast failed for some reason.

fields.name: updateSeriesMetadata
fields.description:
Updates the title and description of a series. A request for this is sent to Opencast,
and the series is preliminarily updated in Tobira's DB.

fields.name: createSeries
fields.description:
Sends an http request to Opencast to create a new series,
and stores the series in Tobira's DB.

fields.name: createPlaylist
fields.description: Creates a new playlist in Opencast and stores it in Tobira's DB.

fields.name: updatePlaylist
fields.description:
Updates a playlist's metadata, entries or acl by sending the changes to Opencast
and updating the playlist in Tobira's DB.

fields.name: deletePlaylist
fields.description: Deletes the given playlist by sending a delete request to Opencast.

fields.name: setChildOrder
fields.description:
Sets the order of all children of a specific realm.

`childIndices` must contain at least one element, i.e. do not call this
for realms without children.

fields.name: renameRealm
fields.description: Changes the name of a realm.

fields.name: updatePermissions
fields.description: Changes the moderator and/or admin roles of a realm.

fields.name: updateRealm
fields.description: Updates a realm's data.

fields.name: removeRealm
fields.description: Remove a realm from the tree.

fields.name: addTitleBlock
fields.description:
Adds a title block to a realm.

The new block will be inserted at the given index,
i.e. it will be at that position after the insert.
Or, if you prefer to think about it this way:
It will be inserted before the block that currently sits
at that index.

fields.name: addTextBlock
fields.description:
Adds a text block to a realm.

See `addTitleBlock` for more details.

fields.name: addSeriesBlock
fields.description:
Adds a series block to a realm.

See `addTitleBlock` for more details.

fields.name: addPlaylistBlock
fields.description:
Adds a playlist block to a realm.

See `addTitleBlock` for more details.

fields.name: addVideoBlock
fields.description:
Adds a video block to a realm.

See `addTitleBlock` for more details.

fields.name: swapBlocksByIndex
fields.description: Swap two blocks.

fields.name: updateTitleBlock
fields.description: Update a title block's data.

fields.name: updateTextBlock
fields.description: Update a text block's data.

fields.name: updateSeriesBlock
fields.description: Update a series block's data.

fields.name: updatePlaylistBlock
fields.description: Update a playlist block's data.

fields.name: updateVideoBlock
fields.description: Update a video block's data.

fields.name: removeBlock
fields.description: Remove a block from a realm.

fields.name: createRealmLineage
fields.description:
Basically `mkdir -p` for realms: makes sure the given realm lineage
exists, creating the missing realms. Existing realms are *not* updated.
Each realm in the given list is the sub-realm of the previous item in
the list. The first item is sub-realm of the root realm.

fields.name: announceSeries
fields.description: Stores series information in Tobira's DB, so it can be mounted without having to be harvested first.

fields.name: addSeriesMountPoint
fields.description: Adds a series block to an empty realm and makes that realm derive its name from said series.

fields.name: removeSeriesMountPoint
fields.description:
Removes the series block of given series from the given realm.
If the realm has sub-realms and used to derive its name from the block,
it is renamed to its path segment. If the realm has no sub-realms,
it is removed completely.
Errors if the given realm does not have exactly one series block referring to the
specified series.

fields.name: mountSeries
fields.description:
Atomically mount a series into an (empty) realm.
Creates all the necessary realms on the path to the target
and adds a block with the given series at the leaf.

fields.name: dummy
fields.description:
Unused dummy field for this marker type. GraphQL requires all objects to
have at least one field. Always returns `null`.

types.name: PlainRealmName
types.description: A simple realm name: a fixed string.

types.name: PlaylistBlock
types.description: A block just showing the list of videos in an Opencast playlist

fields.name: duration
fields.description: How long searching took in ms.

fields.name: rootRealm
fields.description: Returns the main root realm.

fields.name: realmById
fields.description:
Returns the realm with the specific ID or `None` if the ID does not
refer to a realm.

fields.name: realmByPath
fields.description:
Returns the realm with the given path or `null` if the path does not
refer to a realm.

Paths with and without trailing slash are accepted and treated equally.
The paths `""` and `"/"` refer to the root realm. All other paths have
to start with `"/"`. Paths starting with `"/@"` are considered user
root realms.

fields.name: eventByOpencastId
fields.description: Returns an event by its Opencast ID.

fields.name: eventById
fields.description: Returns an event by its ID.

fields.name: seriesByOpencastId
fields.description: Returns a series by its Opencast ID.

fields.name: seriesById
fields.description: Returns a series by its ID.

fields.name: playlistByOpencastId
fields.description: Returns a playlist by its Opencast ID.

fields.name: playlistById
fields.description: Returns a playlist by its ID.

fields.name: currentUser
fields.description: Returns the current user.

fields.name: eventReadJwts
fields.description:
Returns one JWT for each given event (by Opencast IDs), granting the
bearer read access to that event. Events that the user is not allowed
to read will not appear in the resulting list.

fields.name: serviceJwt
fields.description:
Returns a new JWT that can be used to authenticate against Opencast for
using the given service. For `service = Editor`, `event` has to be
specified.

fields.name: node
fields.description: Retrieve a node by globally unique ID. Mostly useful for relay.

fields.name: search
fields.description: Returns `null` if the query is too short.

fields.name: searchAllEvents
fields.description:
Searches through events. Results include:

- Events that the user has write access to (listed & unlisted).
- If `writable_only` is false, this also searches through videos that
  the user has preview access to. However, unless the user has the
  privilege to find unlisted events, only listed ones are searched.

fields.name: searchAllSeries
fields.description:
Searches through series. Searches through:

- Series that the user has write access to (listed & unlisted).
- If `writable_only` is false, this also searches through listed series.
  If the user has the privilege to find unlisted series, all series are
  searched.

fields.name: searchAllPlaylists
fields.description:
Searches through playlists. Results may include:

- Playlists that the user has write access to (listed & unlisted).
- If `writable_only` is false, this also searches through listed playlists.
  If the user has the privilege to find unlisted playlists, all playlists are
  searched.

fields.name: searchKnownUsers
fields.description:
Searches through all known users. The behavior of this depends on the
`general.users_searchable` config value. If it is `false`, this returns
only users that have an exact match with the input query. The number of
results is limited to some fixed value.

fields.name: knownGroups
fields.description: Returns all known groups selectable in the ACL UI.

fields.name: adminDashboardInfo
fields.description: Returns information for the admin dashboard.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The name of this realm or `null` if there is no name (for some reason).
To find out why a realm has no name, you have to check `name_source`
which gives you the raw information about the realm name.

fields.name: nameSource
fields.description:
The raw information about the name of the realm, showing where the name
is coming from and if there is no name, why that is. Can be `null` only for the
root realm, must be non-null for all other realms.

fields.name: isMainRoot
fields.description: Returns `true` if this is the root of the public realm tree (with path = "/").

fields.name: isUserRoot
fields.description: Returns true if this is the root of a user realm tree.

fields.name: isUserRealm
fields.description: Returns `true` if this realm is managed by a user (path starting with `/@`).

fields.name: childOrder
fields.description:
Specifies how the children of this realm should be ordered (e.g. in the
navigation list). That's the responsibility of the frontend.

fields.name: pathSegment
fields.description:
Returns the trailing segment of this realm's path, without any instances of `/`.
Empty for the main root realm.

fields.name: path
fields.description:
Returns the full path of this realm. `"/"` for the main root realm.
Otherwise it never has a trailing `/`. For user realms, starts with
`/@`.

fields.name: ownerDisplayName
fields.description:
This only returns a value for root user realms, in which case it is
the display name of the user who owns this realm. For all other realms,
`null` is returned.

fields.name: nav
fields.description: Info about the navigation UI for this realm.

fields.name: ownAcl
fields.description:
Returns the acl of this realm, combining moderator and admin roles and assigns
the respective actions that are necessary for UI purposes.

fields.name: inheritedAcl
fields.description:
Returns the combined acl of this realm's parent, which effectively contains
the acl and inherited acl of each ancestor realm. This is used to display
these roles in the permissions UI, where we don't want to show that realm's own
flattened acl since that also contains the realm's "regular", i.e. non-inherited
acl.

fields.name: parent
fields.description: Returns the immediate parent of this realm.

fields.name: ancestors
fields.description:
Returns all ancestors between the root realm to this realm
(excluding both, the root realm and this realm). It starts with a
direct child of the root and ends with the parent of `self`.

fields.name: children
fields.description:
Returns all immediate children of this realm. The children are always
ordered by the internal index. If `childOrder` returns an ordering
different from `BY_INDEX`, the frontend is supposed to sort the
children.

fields.name: blocks
fields.description: Returns the (content) blocks of this realm.

fields.name: numberOfDescendants
fields.description:
Returns the number of realms that are descendants of this one
(excluding this one). Returns a number ≥ 0.

fields.name: isCurrentUserPageAdmin
fields.description:
Returns whether the current user has the rights to add sub-pages, edit realm content,
and edit settings including changing the realm path, deleting the realm and editing
the realm's acl.

fields.name: canCurrentUserModerate
fields.description:
Returns whether the current user has the rights to add sub-pages and edit realm content
and non-critical settings.

types.name: RealmNameFromBlock
types.description: A realm name that is derived from a block of that realm.

types.name: RealmNav
types.description: Information to render the navigation for a single realm.

fields.name: header
fields.description:
Elements above the list, usually current page and parent. Is either
0, 1 or 2 elements long. Order is "reversed" in that the last element
is rendered first/topmost. The main root realm is treated as parent of
user root realms.

fields.name: list
fields.description:
Main part of the nav: list of realms to navigate to. These are usually
the children of the current realm, except for non-root leaf nodes, where
it's the siblings (including itself) instead.

fields.name: listOrder
fields.description: Dictates in what order the items in `list` should be displayed.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Resolved name, like `Realm.name`.

types.name: RoleInfo
types.description: Some extra information we know about a role.

fields.name: label
fields.description:
A user-facing label for this role (group or person). If the label does
not depend on the language (e.g. a name), `{ "default": "Peter" }` is
returned.

fields.name: implies
fields.description:
For user roles this is `null`. For groups, it defines a list of other
group roles that this role implies. I.e. a user with this role always
also has these other roles.

fields.name: large
fields.description:
Is `true` if this role represents a large group. Used to warn users
accidentally giving write access to large groups.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: How long searching took in ms.

fields.name: dummy
fields.description:
Unused dummy field for this marker type. GraphQL requires all objects to
have at least one field. Always returns `null`.

types.name: Series
types.description: Represents an Opencast series.

fields.name: numVideos
fields.description:
Returns the number of entries in this series. Note: this is lazily loaded
and only available in certain contexts (e.g., series listings).

fields.name: thumbnailStack
fields.description:
Returns a stack of thumbnails from the events in this series.
This is lazily loaded and pre-loaded in certain contexts (like in `load_writable_for_user`).
In other contexts the thumbnails will be fetched from the database on demand.

fields.name: canWrite
fields.description: Whether the current user has write access to this series.

fields.name: isReferencedByRealm
fields.description:
Returns `true` if the realm has a series block with this series.
Otherwise, `false` is returned.

types.name: SeriesBlock
types.description: A block just showing the list of videos in an Opencast series

fields.name: duration
fields.description: How long searching took in ms.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Duration in ms.

types.name: TextBlock
types.description: A block just showing some text.

types.name: TextMatch
types.description: A match inside an event's texts while searching.

fields.name: start
fields.description:
Start of this timespan in number of milliseconds from the beginning of
the video.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Duration of this timespan in number of milliseconds.

fields.name: text
fields.description:
The text containing the match, with some context. Is `null` if the user
is not allowed to read the event, but only preview it.

fields.name: ty
fields.description: Source of this text.

fields.name: highlights
fields.description: Parts of `text` that should be highlighted.

types.name: ThumbnailInfo
types.description: Information necessary to render a thumbnail.

types.name: TitleBlock
types.description: A block just showing some title.

fields.name: username
fields.description: The username, a unique string identifying the user.

fields.name: roles
fields.description:
Roles of the user. Note: the frontend should not do any role matching itself,
but should rely on Boolean API endpoints like `canUpload` or `event.canWrite`.
This endpoint is only for debugging and for special cases like the ACL selector.

fields.name: userRole
fields.description:
Returns the *user role* of this user. Each user has exactly one and this
role is used in ACLs to give access to a single user. This role is
always also contained in `roles`.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: The name of the user intended to be read by humans.

fields.name: userRealmHandle
fields.description:
The part of the user realm path after `@`, i.e. `/@${user_realm_handle}`.
Equals the username, unless overwritten by the auth integration.

fields.name: canUpload
fields.description: `True` if the user has the permission to upload videos.

fields.name: canUseStudio
fields.description: `True` if the user has the permission to use Opencast Studio.

fields.name: canUseEditor
fields.description: `True` if the user has the permission to use Opencast Editor.

fields.name: canFindUnlisted
fields.description: `True` if the user is allowed to find unlisted items when editing page content.

fields.name: canCreateSeries
fields.description: `True` if the user has the permission to create new series.

fields.name: canCreatePlaylists
fields.description: `True` if the user has the permission to create new playlists.

fields.name: isTobiraAdmin
fields.description:
`True` if user is a global Tobira admin, i.e. having `ROLE_ADMIN` or the
configured Tobira admin role.

fields.name: myVideos
fields.description:
Returns all events that somehow "belong" to the user, i.e. that appear
on the "my videos" page. This also returns events that have been marked
as deleted (meaning their deletion in Opencast has been requested but they
are not yet removed from Tobira's database).

fields.name: mySeries
fields.description:
Returns all series that somehow "belong" to the user, i.e. that appear
on the "my series" page.

fields.name: myPlaylists
fields.description:
Returns all playlists that somehow "belong" to the user, i.e. that appear
on the "my playlists" page.

types.name: VideoBlock
types.description: A block for presenting a single Opencast event

types.name: SearchOutcome
types.description:
Return type of the search API. `EmptyQuery` is only returned if the passed
search query is empty. `SearchUnavailable` is returned if the backend
search service is, for some reason, not available. Otherwise
`SearchResults` is returned.
